title: Slot-aware batch fusion experiment diary
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is an experimental notebook-style writeup of a set of microbenchmarks and multi-GPU integration tests for a new scheduling idea: slot-aware batch fusion. Goal: reduce short-term interconnect contention and tail latency for small, bursty inference arrivals by fusing small batches into larger GPU-friendly batches while intentionally staggering collective communication windows across replicas (so we don't have all-replicas hitting NVLink/NIC at the same instant).

High-level idea:
- Traditional batching: collect requests until a size or timeout and run a single forward. When many replicas run the fused batch at the same time, NCCL collectives (allreduce/allgather for shard sync, or parameter broadcast/kv-sync) can align and produce short bursts of interconnect saturation (microbursts) that amplify tail latency.
- Slot-aware fusion: assign fused-batch executions to logical time slots per replica such that collective phases are offset. Within a single rack / host, neighbors are assigned alternating slots. Fusion still preserves per-request ordering and max wait-time.

Hypotheses we wanted to test:
1) Offsetting collective windows should reduce instantaneous link utilization peaks by spreading work over time, lowering p99 tail latency for short requests (<=128 tokens).
2) Fusion increases average throughput for small payloads by improving GPU occupancy; combined with slotting it should avoid worsening tail when traffic is bursty.
3) There will be a tradeoff: increased mean latency for some percentiles (due to waiting for assigned slot) vs reduced p99 from lower contention.

Hardware / topology / infra used:
- Cluster: 8-node test rack, each node: 8xA100-40GB, NVLink within node, HDR200 interconnect across nodes using RoCE.
- Model: Llama-like decoder-only 19B, 32-bit activations, 4-way tensor-parallel + 2-way pipeline-parallel logical partitioning (per replica).
- Serving runtime: latest branch with fusion layer + slot scheduler (PR linked above). Runtime flags: --fusion-timeout-ms=10, --max-fused-requests=8, --slot-window-ms=5, --slot-count=4
- Load generator: synthetic arrival traces derived from production x-request trace (subsampled), two modes: poisson-smooth and bursty-peaky (bursts of 200 reqs within 100ms).

Benchmarks and metrics collected:
- Throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec)
- Latency percentiles: p50, p90, p95, p99, p99.9 for end-to-end inference (client to response)
- Per-GPU kernel occupancy and utilization (nvidia-smi sampling + nvprof traces)
- Interconnect bytes/sec by link (collected via NIC counters + custom perfmon for NVLink)
- NCCL telemetry: collective start/end timestamps, bytes, proto (allreduce/allgather)
- CPU scheduling and queueing times (host staging latency)

Experiment matrix (shortened):
- Baseline: no fusion, standard batching (timeout=2ms, max_batch=8)
- Fusion-only: fusion enabled, no slotting (same timeout/max_batch)
- Slot-aware fusion: fusion enabled with slot_count=4 and slot_window=5ms, two placement strategies: rack-aware alternating and random-slot assignment
- Burst intensity sweep: burst sizes [50, 100, 200, 500]
- Replica counts: 2, 4, 8 replicas (within rack and cross-rack)

Key empirical observations:
1) Peak link utilization smoothing:
- Baseline: moments of >92% link utilization across all racks during bursts (spikes last 3-12ms).
- Fusion-only: average link utilization increased (more bytes/s) but spikes stayed aligned, leading to slightly worse p99 in heavy bursts.
- Slot-aware fusion (rack-alternating): peak instantaneous utilization dropped by ~28% during bursts; spikes elongated but lower magnitude.

2) Tail latency behavior:
- For poisson-smooth traces, fusion-only improved mean latency and p50/p90 by ~10-18% vs baseline. p99 unchanged.
- For bursty traces, fusion-only increased p99 by ~12% (due to synchronized collectives).
- Slot-aware fusion improved p99 by 22% vs fusion-only under bursty traces, and by 8% vs baseline in the same condition. p99.9 improvements were visible but volatile (noisy).

3) Throughput and GPU efficiency:
- Fusion (both variants) increased GPU occupancy and tokens/sec by ~15% for small requests (<=128 tokens).
- Slotting introduced negligible throughput loss (<2%) for moderate burst sizes; at extreme bursts (>=500) we saw ~5% throughput drop for rack-alternating slot assignment because some slots became locally overloaded when placement skewed. Random-slot assignment smoothed that but had marginally worse p99 than rack-alternating.

4) NCCL behavior and microburst causes:
- We observed that when many replicas begin the collective in the same 1-3ms window, NIC buffers hit headroom limits and RoCE retransmits introduced latency amplification. Spreading collective start times reduced retransmits and breathing-room pressure.
- Intra-node NVLink behaves differently: NVLink has more aggregate bandwidth, so per-node spacing had smaller effect; cross-node collectives were the main cause of p99 spikes.

5) Host staging and CPU-side queueing:
- Slot-aware scheduler increased host-side waiting time by the slot window (by design). For low concurrency this was measurable (+3-6ms median). When fused batch sizes were high enough, CPU staging amortized so median latency returned close to baseline.

Config-level notes that mattered:
- slot_window_ms should be small (3-10ms). Too small -> ineffective offsetting, too large -> wasted user-visible wait. We found 4-7ms sweet spot for our topology and model.
- slot_count tuned to number of hot replicas in the switching domain (typically 4 for 8-GPU hosts across 2 nodes). Over-partitioning increases scheduling churn with diminishing returns.
- Fusion timeout needs to be adaptive: static 10ms is ok for our load, but during severe tails adaptive timeout that short-circuits fusion when backlog zero improves p99.

Interesting failure modes and caveats:
- If slot assignment is static and traffic pattern is skewed (one host receives 60% of traffic), the slotting can concentrate collectives on the same slot repeatedly and worsen local contention. Need periodic slot rebalancing or randomized jitter.
- Heterogeneous interconnect: mixed racks with older HDR links saw less benefit from slotting (link saturation points are asymmetric). We need topology-aware slot placement (prefer longer-slot separation across weaker links).
- Some models with heavy KV-cache traffic have collectives at different phases; slotting must coordinate both model-shard sync and KV-coherence windows to be effective.

Quick experiment logs (timestamps are local test lab):
- 2024-11-18 09:12: baseline run (poisson) -> p99 38ms, throughput 18k tok/s
- 2024-11-18 11:05: fusion-only (poisson) -> p99 36ms, p95 12ms, throughput 21k tok/s
- 2024-12-02 14:30: bursty (200) baseline -> p99 112ms, spikes coincident with collectives
- 2024-12-02 15:10: fusion-only bursty -> p99 125ms, more frequent retransmits observed on NIC counters
- 2024-12-03 10:05: slot-aware rack-alternating bursty -> p99 98ms, spike magnitude reduced, overall smoother link graphs
- 2025-01-09 16:22: slot-aware random-slot extreme burst 500 -> throughput -5%, p99 fluctuating 140-200ms (noisy), JVM/nic telemetry shows transient backpressure

Profiling notes and commands used:
- Collected NCCL events via NCCL_TESTS and our patched runtime (timestamps logged to /tmp/nccl-trace). Grep for overlapping start times to compute simultaneous collectives.
- NIC counters via ethtool -S and vendor perfmon; NVLink counters via nvidia-smi --query-gpu=... with sampling.
- Kernel traces captured with perf and combined with GPU trace to align host-collective windows.

Open action items and next steps:
- Add adaptive slot sizing: detect per-link saturation and dynamically widen slots for congested links.
- Integrate slot-aware placement into router: route requests to replicas with complementary slot assignments when low-latency SLAs apply.
- Implement periodic slot-randomization/jitter to avoid static-skew pathological cases.
- Run the same test on cloud heterogeneous topologies (mix of V100/A100 and mixed NVLink configs) and capture variance.
- Validate with production trace for 7 days to ensure no regression on tail metrics for real traffic.

Unresolved questions we should answer experimentally:
- What is the minimal slot_window_ms that still reduces RoCE retransmits across different payload sizes?
- For pipeline-parallel models with multi-stage cross-stage comm, how to align stage boundaries with slots without introducing stage-level stalls?
- How does slot-aware fusion interact with autoscaling/autobursting that can change replica counts at runtime?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a lab-level experiment with synthetic and replayed traces. Results are sensitive to link probe fidelity and NIC counters accuracy.
- If we want to pursue in prod: add telemetry hooks (collective start histograms) and a canary phase on a small dedicated cluster before rolling to Dedicated customers.

Random brainstorm bullets:
- Could do slot layering: short slot to break collectives, and long slot to spread heavier KV-sync windows on different timescales.
- Combine with probabilistic fusion: only fuse if downstream replica is in a complementary slot to avoid synchronized collectives.
- Explore using RDMA priority flow control (PFC) knobs to soften retransmit behavior as complementary lever.

Appendix: raw numbers sample (single run, bursty200, 4 replicas)
- Baseline p50/p90/p99: 12ms / 46ms / 112ms
- Fusion-only p50/p90/p99: 9ms / 38ms / 125ms
- Slot-aware p50/p90/p99: 11ms / 34ms / 98ms
- Average link instantaneous peak (bytes/sec): baseline 640GB/s, fusion-only 780GB/s (aligned spikes), slot-aware 560GB/s (spread)

If useful I'll convert selected charts into the perf dashboard and attach the CSVs. Feedback welcome, especially on: best heuristics for slot rebalancing; whether to expose slot parameters as per-customer policy (allow higher wait for guaranteed lower p99), and how to synthesize slot-aware placement into the router without exploding state.

Footer: experimental draft by Asha (eng-serving-runtime).
